description: Foundry M0 frozen baseline for the Arena Training Builder (Program Authorship). Cases are workplace-training intents written as a manager would enter them. Clinical cases name a workflow step only; they deliberately define no clinical criteria, protocol or standard of care.
source_bounds: Every fact a generated program may rely on is in the case's answers. Nothing else is known. Material text restates the intent; it is not a clinical or policy source.

answers.title: Senior review before the final impression
answers.problem: Newer doctors sometimes take the final impression for a crown without anyone else looking at the preparation first, and problems are found only when the crown comes back.
answers.audienceDetail: Associate doctors in their first year
answers.recurringMoment: When a crown preparation is finished and the final impression is next
answers.observableBehavior: Ask a senior doctor to look at the preparation before taking the final impression.
answers.successEvidence: The senior doctor confirms they were asked to look before the impression was taken.
answers.materialText: This training is about the review step only: asking a senior doctor to look before the final impression. It does not set out any clinical criteria for the preparation itself; those come from the clinic's own clinical leads.

answers.title: Explain what happens next
answers.problem: Patients leave the chair unsure what the next step of their care is, and call the front desk later to ask.
answers.recurringMoment: At the end of an appointment, before the patient leaves the chair
answers.observableBehavior: Tell the patient in one or two plain sentences what happens next and when.
answers.successEvidence: A colleague hears the patient told what happens next before they leave the chair.
answers.materialText: Patients should not have to call back to find out their next step. Before they leave the chair, say what happens next and when, in plain words.

answers.title: Share the cost before the plan is agreed
answers.problem: Treatment plans are sometimes agreed before the patient has heard what it will cost, and the cost conversation then happens at the front desk.
answers.recurringMoment: When presenting a treatment plan to a patient
answers.observableBehavior: State the estimated cost of the plan before asking the patient to agree to it.
answers.successEvidence: The patient hears the estimated cost before they are asked to agree to the plan.
answers.materialText: The cost belongs in the plan conversation, not after it. Say the estimated cost before asking for agreement.

answers.title: One owner for every open item
answers.problem: Morning huddles end with agreement, but nobody clearly owns the next action, so items carry over for days.
answers.recurringMoment: At the end of the morning huddle when there are open items
answers.observableBehavior: Name one owner and a time for each open item before the huddle ends.
answers.successEvidence: Each open item has a named owner and a time when the huddle ends.
answers.materialText: An item without an owner is an item nobody will do. Before the huddle ends, each open item gets one name and one time.

answers.title: Clear handoff between assistants
answers.problem: When an assistant hands a room over mid-shift, the incoming assistant often does not know what is still pending for the patient.
answers.recurringMoment: When handing a room over to another assistant during a shift
answers.observableBehavior: Tell the incoming assistant what is still pending for the patient before leaving the room.
answers.successEvidence: The incoming assistant can say what is still pending for the patient after the handoff.
answers.materialText: A handoff is finished when the next person knows what is still pending, not when the first person leaves.

answers.title: Give feedback on the day it happens
answers.problem: Team leads wait days to mention a problem with someone's work, and by then the person does not remember the situation.
answers.recurringMoment: When a team lead notices a problem with a team member's work
answers.observableBehavior: Speak privately with the team member the same day and describe what you saw.
answers.successEvidence: The team member says they heard about it the same day it happened.
answers.materialText: Feedback is easiest to use while the moment is still fresh. Describe what you saw, privately, the same day.

answers.title: Say it when the schedule is slipping
answers.problem: When the schedule runs late, staff quietly rush and nobody tells the front desk, so waiting patients are not informed.
answers.recurringMoment: When an appointment is running more than fifteen minutes late
answers.observableBehavior: Tell the front desk how late the schedule is running so waiting patients can be informed.
answers.successEvidence: The front desk confirms they were told the schedule was running late.
answers.materialText: Rushing silently does not help waiting patients. Tell the front desk how late things are running so they can tell patients.

answers.title: Note the next visit before closing the record
answers.problem: Visit notes are closed without recording what the next visit is for, so the next provider has to work it out again.
answers.recurringMoment: When closing a patient's visit notes
answers.observableBehavior: Write what the next visit is for before closing the visit notes.
answers.successEvidence: The next provider finds the purpose of the next visit written in the notes.
answers.materialText: The next provider should not have to reconstruct the plan. Write what the next visit is for before you close the notes.

answers.title: Check in with a new hire at the end of their day
answers.problem: New employees finish their first weeks without anyone asking what confused them, and small questions become bigger mistakes.
answers.recurringMoment: At the end of a new employee's working day during their first two weeks
answers.observableBehavior: Ask the new employee what was unclear today and answer one of their questions.
answers.successEvidence: The new employee says someone asked them what was unclear that day.
answers.materialText: A new person rarely asks unprompted. A short question at the end of the day catches confusion early.

answers.title: Raise it before the end of the shift
answers.problem: Staff notice problems that need a manager's decision but wait until the next day to mention them, and the problem grows overnight.
answers.recurringMoment: When you notice a problem that needs a manager's decision
answers.observableBehavior: Tell the manager on duty about the problem before your shift ends.
answers.successEvidence: The manager on duty says they heard about the problem before the shift ended.
answers.materialText: A problem that needs a decision should reach someone who can decide it on the same shift.

answers.title: Call back when you said you would
answers.problem: Staff promise patients a call back with an answer, then the call does not happen when it was promised.
answers.recurringMoment: When you promise a patient a call back
answers.observableBehavior: Tell the patient the time you will call back and call them by that time.
answers.successEvidence: The patient receives the call back by the time they were given.
answers.materialText: A promised call is a commitment. Give a time you can keep, then keep it.

answers.title: Ask a quiet teammate for their view
answers.problem: In team meetings the same few people speak, and quieter teammates' concerns come out later, after decisions are made.
answers.recurringMoment: During a team meeting before a decision is made
answers.observableBehavior: Ask a teammate who has not spoken yet for their view before the decision is made.
answers.successEvidence: A teammate who had not spoken is asked for their view before the decision.
answers.materialText: Decisions are better when the quieter people have been heard. Ask them before deciding, not after.

answers.title: Tell the patient before anything touches them
answers.problem: Patients are startled when an instrument or water is used without warning.
answers.audienceDetail: Clinical team members who work chairside
answers.recurringMoment: Right before starting a step that the patient will feel
answers.observableBehavior: Tell the patient what they are about to feel before starting the step.
answers.successEvidence: A colleague hears the patient told what they will feel before the step starts.
answers.materialText: A short warning makes a step easier for the patient. Say what they will feel before you start.

answers.title: Ask for help early in a difficult preparation
answers.problem: A newer doctor keeps going alone when a crown preparation is not going as expected, and asks for help only when the appointment is already running over.
answers.audienceDetail: Associate doctors in their first year
answers.recurringMoment: When a crown preparation is not going as expected partway through
answers.observableBehavior: Ask a senior doctor to come to the room as soon as the preparation is not going as expected.
answers.successEvidence: The senior doctor confirms they were asked to come while the preparation was still underway.
answers.materialText: This training is only about asking for help early. It does not describe how the preparation should be done or judged; that is for the clinic's clinical leads.

answers.title: Check what the patient understood
answers.problem: After a treatment plan is explained, patients agree but later show they did not understand the main steps.
answers.recurringMoment: After explaining a treatment plan to a patient
answers.observableBehavior: Ask the patient to say back the main steps of the plan in their own words.
answers.successEvidence: The patient says back the main steps of the plan in their own words.
answers.materialText: Agreement is not the same as understanding. A short say-back shows whether the plan landed.

answers.title: Close the loop on lab cases
answers.problem: Lab cases are sent out but nobody checks they are back before the patient's appointment, so appointments are wasted.
answers.recurringMoment: Two days before an appointment that needs a lab case
answers.observableBehavior: Check that the lab case has arrived and tell the doctor if it has not.
answers.successEvidence: The doctor hears whether the lab case has arrived two days before the appointment.
answers.materialText: A missing lab case found on the day costs the patient a visit. Check two days before and say so if it is not there.

answers.title: 회의 끝에 담당자 정하기
answers.problem: 아침 회의가 끝나도 누가 무엇을 할지 정해지지 않아 같은 일이 며칠씩 남아 있다.
answers.recurringMoment: 아침 회의가 끝날 때 남은 일이 있을 때
answers.observableBehavior: 회의가 끝나기 전에 남은 일마다 담당자 한 명과 완료 시간을 정한다.
answers.successEvidence: 회의가 끝날 때 남은 일마다 담당자와 완료 시간이 정해져 있다.
answers.materialText: 담당자가 없는 일은 아무도 하지 않는다. 회의가 끝나기 전에 일마다 이름 하나와 시간 하나를 정한다.

answers.title: 업무 인계 확인하기
answers.problem: 업무를 인계한 뒤 서로 확인하지 않아 중요한 일이 빠진다.
answers.recurringMoment: 업무를 다른 사람에게 넘길 때
answers.observableBehavior: 업무를 넘길 때 해야 할 일과 완료 시점을 말하고 상대가 이해한 내용을 한 번 확인한다.
answers.successEvidence: 업무를 받은 사람이 해야 할 일과 완료 시점을 말할 수 있다.
answers.materialText: 인계는 다음 사람이 해야 할 일을 알 때 끝난다. 넘기기 전에 한 번 확인한다.

answers.title: 치료 전에 비용 먼저 설명하기
answers.problem: 치료가 시작된 뒤에야 환자가 비용을 듣고 놀라는 일이 있다.
answers.recurringMoment: 치료를 시작하기 전에 환자와 이야기할 때
answers.observableBehavior: 치료를 시작하기 전에 환자에게 예상 비용을 먼저 말한다.
answers.successEvidence: 환자가 치료 시작 전에 예상 비용을 들었다고 말한다.
answers.materialText: 비용은 치료 전에 듣는 것이 환자에게 공정하다. 시작하기 전에 예상 비용을 말한다.

answers.title: Practice Living with Belief
answers.problem: 신념을 가지고 살면 좋겠어.
answers.recurringMoment: during team discussions or meetings
answers.observableBehavior: shares personal beliefs and values openly
answers.successEvidence: a colleague hears a team member express their beliefs clearly
answers.materialText: This training is about saying what you believe in a team discussion. It does not prescribe which beliefs are right.
